title: Session‑Resilient Hedge and Recovery Protocol for Hosted Edge
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Our hosted API edge must remain usable during region outages and transient capacity spikes without dropping live streaming sessions or violating tail latency SLOs. Current failover mechanics perform a blunt global cutover which either causes streaming connections to be reset or allows sustained latency/cost regressions when load is shifted to under-provisioned regions. We also lack an integrated, session-aware circuit that can selectively shed load while preserving long‑running conversations and avoiding partial history loss.

Goals:
- Implement a hedging + staged recovery protocol that preserves session continuity for streaming and sessionful requests across active-active regions.
- Provide per-route, per-customer SLO mapping to automated decisions (hedge, shed, divert).
- Add an observable, telemetry-gated circuit that performs graceful degradation rather than abrupt resets.
- Ensure decisions are reversible and safe (no split-brain replays) and provide strong accounting for token/usage billing.

High-level design:
1) Session metadata anchoring: when a session is established at Gateway A, write a lightweight session anchor to the distributed session registry (region‑local + cross‑region tombstone). Anchors include last-acknowledged token index, preferred routing policy, and model variant. The registry is optimized for small writes and eventual cross-region convergence.
2) Hedge-on-degradation: when tail latency or token throughput at the serving tier crosses a configured headroom threshold, the gateway starts parallel hedged requests to a secondary region but attaches a session continuity token. Only the first successful response is returned; secondary responses are used for telemetry and fallback state reconciliation.
3) Stream-preserving handoff: for in-flight streaming sessions, the gateway initiates a short-lived KV checkpoint (partial KV snapshot + recent prefix). If recovery requires a region switch, the handoff copies the checkpoint to the target region and resumes the stream without invalidating already-delivered tokens. Checkpoints are encrypted in transit and TTL-limited.
4) Telemetry-gated circuit: a circuit monitors multi-metric windows (latency p99, queue length, GPU utilization, KV write error rate). Circuits can be graded: soft (reduce new session admits), medium (hedge majority of new requests), hard (reject non-critical requests). Circuit decisions are annotated with SLO budget consumption and customer tier to enable priority-preserving shedding.
5) Consistent billing and idempotency: all hedged or replayed requests include deterministic request ids and reconciliation markers so that billing and token counting are idempotent even when multiple regions return partial outputs.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strong consistency vs availability for session anchors: chose eventual cross-region convergence with tombstoning to avoid global writes on every token. This reduces latency but requires reconciliation on rare divergence cases.
- Cost of hedging: hedging increases token egress and GPU cycles; policy ties hedging to SLO headroom and customer tier to control cost.
- Complexity of stream handoff: adding KV snapshotting increases implementation complexity and storage needs. We limit snapshots to minimal state (KV caches + last 2k tokens) and TTL to bound costs.

Telemetry & SLO mapping:
- SLOs: 99th percentile request latency <= 150ms for non-stream requests, streaming resumption time <= 400ms for streaming handoff.
- KPIs: p50/p95/p99 latency per region, hedged-hit rate, handoff success rate, session-loss incidents, billing idempotency errors.
- Alerts: p99 latency sustained > SLO for 3min triggers "hedge-on-degradation"; handoff failure rate > 0.5% for 10min triggers rollback to prior routing.

Acceptance criteria: (see acceptance_criteria list)

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): enable soft circuits + hedging for 5% of traffic for internal orgs; collect telemetry; no session handoff enabled.
- Phase 2: enable stream checkpointing and handoff for a subset of customers with explicit opt-in; monitor handoff success and billing correctness.
- Phase 3: widen hedging policies, enable automatic graded circuits and per-tenancy priority shedding, roll to 100% for hosted API endpoints.

Testing & Validation:
- Chaos experiments: simulated regional latency spikes, partial KV registry partitions, and synthetic GPU saturation to validate hedging and handoff behavior.
- Integration tests: end-to-end streaming tests across regions to verify resume semantics and token-preservation.
- Load tests: measure cost delta for representative workload with hedging on vs off.

Dependencies: ["ENG-230411","ENG-14257","ENG-704800"], Confluence design: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/EDGE/pages/Session+Resiliency+Design, PR checklist: github.com/redwoodinc/edge/pulls (TBD).
acceptance_criteria: Session anchor writes succeed in <25ms median and converge across regions within 60s under normal network conditions.
Hedged requests reduce p99 latency by at least 25% for targeted canary routes without increasing token billing anomalies.
Stream handoff resumes delivery at target region with <=400ms additional latency and with zero missing tokens in 99.5% of cases.
Circuit state transitions have associated telemetry and can be overridden manually from Console within 1 minute.
No customer experiences a billing duplication incident in canary (billing idempotency error rate <0.01%).
risks: Increased egress and GPU costs from hedging if policy thresholds are too permissive.
Edge cases where session anchor divergence causes transient duplicate state and requires reconciliation.
Operational complexity of per-tenant shedding policies leading to misconfiguration and inadvertent customer impact.
implementation_notes: Start by adding 'session_anchor' proto to gateway control plane and a TTL-backed session registry service with cross-region replication stream.
Implement hedging as an opt-in router middleware that can be toggled via per-route flags in the config service.
Implement small KV snapshot API in runtime to export minimal cache + prefix state for a session in O(1) time relative to token size limit.
Circuit thresholds should be expressed in composite metrics config and wired into existing Console for manual inspection and override.
